prompt_text:
Act as a physics teacher.
- 10 MCQs
- Topic: projectile motion
- Audience: Class 11
- 4 options, A to D
- Only one correct answer, shown in bold
- Explain why the right option is right and the others wrong
- Order from easy to hard

You are a history lecturer. 1. Write 8 questions on the French Revolution for first-year BA students. 2. Each has 4 options labelled 1 to 4. 3. Do not tell the students which option is correct inside the question list; put the key on a separate last page. 4. No basic recall questions.

Act as an economics professor. Create 10 MCQs on elasticity of demand for second-year students. The questions should not be easy; they should be at an expert level. Four options A-D, one right answer only, mark it with a star.
Write MCQs on cell division.

I am a school teacher. Prepare 15 MCQs on fractions for Class 6. They should be very easy. Please skip any basic or recall type questions. Give 4 choices each, labelled a, b, c, d, and put the correct letter in brackets after each question.

You are a philosophy tutor. Set 6 MCQs on utilitarianism for undergraduate students. Make the wording deliberately confusing and tricky. Five options labelled A to E. There can be more than one correct option per question, and students must pick all of them. Say which options are correct at the end of the paper.

Act as a computer networks lecturer. Write 12 MCQs on TCP congestion control for third-year B.Tech students. Four options A-D. Keep the answers hidden until the end of the quiz. After every question, state the correct answer and a one-line reason.

Respected AI, I am teaching accounting to commerce students in first year. Kindly prepare for me twenty MCQ on journal entries. Each have four option marking with A B C D. Only single option is correct. Please give explanation of every option why correct or why not. Start from simple and go to difficult slowly.

As a statistics lecturer, set 10 MCQs on hypothesis testing for MSc students. Make them extremely simple. At the same time they must be advanced, research level questions. Four options A to D, correct answer in bold.

You are a sociology teacher. Write 8 MCQs on social stratification for first-year students. Each question has exactly one right answer. Some questions may also accept more than one answer as correct. Four options A to D.
Act as a chemistry teacher. Make 25 MCQs on the periodic table for Class 10. Four options labelled A, B, C, D. Provide a separate answer key after all the questions.

Act as a biology lecturer. Write 10 MCQs on genetics for B.Sc students with a mix of easy and hard questions in random order. Four options A to D, correct one in bold. Explain only the correct answer.
Act as a law lecturer. Write 10 MCQs on tort law for LLB students, starting with the hardest and ending with the easiest. Four options A to D, one correct answer in bold.
Sir please make MCQ paper on Indian Constitution for class 12. 20 question, 4 option each, answer will be given at the end of paper, not with question.

Act as an electronics lecturer. Write 10 MCQs on transistor biasing for diploma students with four options each labelled A to D, mark the correct option with a tick, and explain why each option is right or wrong.

You are a management teacher. Create 10 MCQs on Maslow's hierarchy for MBA students. Do not use tricky or confusing wording; keep the language plain. Four options A to D, with exactly one correct answer in bold. Questions should go from easiest to hardest.
Act as a primary school teacher. Write 10 very easy MCQs on the water cycle for Class 3. Three options each, labelled A, B, C. Show the correct answer in bold and explain it in one sentence.
As an advanced algorithms professor, write 8 expert-level MCQs on dynamic programming for PhD students. Four options A to D, one correct answer.
Create a quiz for my class about the solar system. Make it fun and not boring.
Act as a mechanical engineering professor. Write 12 MCQs on thermodynamic cycles for final-year students. Four options A to D. Do not include questions that only test basic recall or definitions.

You are a Python instructor. Write 10 MCQs on list comprehensions for beginner programmers, four options A to D. Right after each question, give the correct answer and a short explanation of why the others are wrong.
Act as a geography teacher. Write 15 MCQs on monsoons for Class 9. Each question has just one correct option. Do not print the answers in the questions section; give them in a table at the end.

You are a literature professor. Write 6 MCQs on symbolism in Hamlet for MA students, four options A to D, where several options may be defensible and more than one can be correct. Mark all acceptable options.
Act as a logic teacher. Write 10 MCQs on syllogisms for BA students with intentionally tricky, confusing phrasing. Four options A to D, one correct answer underlined. Order from easy to hard.

I coordinate the medicine module on cardiology for fourth-year students and I would like you to take the role of an experienced consultant who also teaches. Prepare 30 multiple-choice questions about heart failure. Each question must have five options labelled A to E with a single best answer. Questions should be easy at first and become progressively harder. After each question please reveal the answer along with the reasoning for every option.
20 MCQs on sorting algorithms, 4 options, bold the answer.
Act as a language teacher. Write 10 very easy MCQs on English prepositions for Class 5. Four options A to D, one correct answer in bold. Put all the answers in an answer key at the end.
Act as a finance lecturer. Write 10 MCQs on bond pricing for undergraduates. Very easy for everyone, yet expert level, and with no basic questions. Four options A to D.
Act as a marketing teacher. Write 10 MCQs on the 4Ps for BBA students. Four options A to D, exactly one correct, bold. The answers should not be hidden: show them immediately after each question.
Prepare a quiz paper for Class 7 maths with 12 questions on ratios, each question with four choices numbered 1 to 4, answers listed after the last question, simple to complex order.
